messages:
ana: Quick sync — pushing a small UX tweak proposal for automatic fallback policies. Idea: show a compact "fallback affordance" inline on a rollout card that summarizes degrade mode, trigger class, and a one-click runbook link.

mike: Love the idea. Can you sketch the fields you want to show? We need to avoid clutter on the rollout list.

jess: +1 for runbook link. Also we need an explicit audit-id surface so SRE/CS can trace incidents.

ana (typo fix)???

ana: whoops, meant ana: Sketch: 
- mode: quiet-degrade / redirect / synthetic-response
- trigger: error-class (5xx spike / latency pctile / custom tag)
- sampling: 1% / 10% / 100%
- fallback-model: small-lm-v1
- audit id (uuid) with copy button
- "Open runbook" (links to runbook + runbook playback e.g., pre-filled query)

mike: That lets operators reason quickly. For triggers: can we show the last matching telemetry point? e.g., "last_trigger: 2026-03-21 14:03 UTC — 5xx: 12% (5m)"

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout/rdw-1234 created by ana; policy=auto-fallback; id=rdw-1234; status=staged

jess: Telemetry inline is good, but be careful of racing: the rollout card should show a stable snapshot (what was true at policy evaluation time) and then a live badge separate from audit snapshot.

sam: UX question: when an operator clicks the runbook, do we want a guided action (eg: "ramp down sample", "escalate to oncall") or just docs? Guided actions require extra guardrails.

ana (again typo)??

ana: ana: Good call — I propose runbook starts as a doc with quick actions collapsed behind an "operator mode" (togglable). Actions require a confirmation modal and will log an operator action id. That action id should be included in the audit trail.

lee: Another requirement: quota interactions. If fallback increases cost (bigger model), show an estimated delta and which quota bucket it will draw from. We had confusion last month when a fallback pushed traffic to dedicated fleet.

mike: Right. Minimal mock of card UI (text):
```
Rollout rdw-1234 — auto-fallback
mode: quiet-degrade  | trigger: 5xx_spike(>10%) | sample: 5%
fallback: small-lm-v1 (est +0.8$ / 1000 tokens)
audit: a1b2c3d4 · last_snapshot: 2026-03-21T14:03Z
[Open runbook] [Preview fallback sample] [Escalate]
```

jess: We should include a compact "why did fallback fire" link which opens the causal trace (error -> route -> policy match). That helps product repro steps.

ops-bot: telemetry-bot: sample_event logged: audit=a1b2c3d4 event=fallback_triggered trigger=5xx_spike pct=12 sample=5%

sam: On the audit side: ensure the audit record stores both the policy version and the model variant used, plus the operator action id if present. Also store the input prompt hash or pointer for reproducibility (privacy-safe).

ana (typo)??

ana: ana: Noted. I'll update the policy schema draft to include: policy_version, trigger_snapshot (metrics), fallback_variant, operator_action_id, input_ref (hash or s3 pointer), cost_estimate, quota_bucket.

lee: Small ask — add a "rollback preview" that shows how long the system kept fallback active historically for similar triggers (avg duration). That helps oncall decide whether to wait it out.

mike: Implementation concerns: we need to plumb the policy evaluation timestamp into the rollout object and ensure the console caches snapshots for playback to avoid live mutation. Backend: store evaluation_snapshot in rollout_history table as JSON blob (bounded TTL). UX: show "snapshot" vs "live" toggle.

jess: Also think about permissioning — the one-click actions should be gated to a role with "operator" scope, and every click must produce an audit event with the user id and action id.

ana (typo)??

ana: ana: agree. I'll draft the console changes + API contract. Quick API sketch: POST /rollouts/{id}/actions { "action": "escalate", "comment": "..." } -> returns action_id. We'll record action_id in audit blob.

sam: Can you include a minimal example of the audit blob shape so security/compliance can review?

ana: sure, rough example (privacy-safe, flattened strings):
```
{
  "policy_version": "v3.2.1",
  "evaluation_ts": "2026-03-21T14:03:05Z",
  "trigger": "5xx_spike",
  "trigger_metrics": "5m: 12%",
  "fallback_variant": "small-lm-v1",
  "operator_action_id": "act-20260321-77",
  "input_ref": "sha256:abcd...",
  "cost_estimate": "$0.8/1k",
  "quota_bucket": "dedicated-gpu-pool"
}
```

jess: That looks reasonable. Compliance will ask for retention policy; recommend TTL 90 days for detailed blobs, with an aggregated long-term index for audit queries.

ana: I'll add TTL notes. Next steps: ana will push a console mock, mike will estimate backend storage/throughput impact, sam will draft an RBAC matrix, jess will loop in security/compliance, lee will gather quota mapping.

mike: I'll run a quick perf calc: if we snapshot 1KB per evaluation and we have 100K evaluations/day, that's ~100MB/day — acceptable. Need to ensure we index by audit id for playback queries.

ops-bot: calendar-bot: meeting scheduled by ana for 2026-03-23 16:00 UTC (30m) — "Fallback affordance sync"

ana: thanks all — I'll put the mock and the API sketch in the design doc and share before the meeting. :thumbsup:

lee: thanks — will bring quota mapping notes.

jess: thanks, all.
